# proxmox_firewall_rules (Data Source)

Lists the firewall rules of one ruleset in their effective order, the same scopes `proxmox_firewall_rule` writes. `pos` and `digest` identify a rule, `pending` does not exist because Proxmox keeps firewall rules un-staged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Cluster ruleset (the default scope).
data "proxmox_firewall_rules" "cluster" {}

# Rules of one guest.
data "proxmox_firewall_rules" "vm100" {
  scope      = "guest"
  node       = "pve-1"
  guest_type = "qemu"
  vmid       = 100
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `guest_type` (String) `qemu` or `lxc` for the `guest` scope.
- `node` (String) Node name for the `node` and `guest` scopes.
- `scope` (String) Ruleset scope: `cluster` (default), `node`, `guest`, `security_group`, or `vnet`.
- `security_group` (String) Security group name for the `security_group` scope.
- `vmid` (Number) Guest VMID for the `guest` scope.
- `vnet` (String) SDN VNet for the `vnet` scope.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this data source call.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Rules in their effective order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
